questions.q: What does Catmull say matters more than a great idea?
a: A great team that communicates well
A large budget and famous actors
A strict deadline and clear rules
A single brilliant leader
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a mediocre idea given to a brilliant team can become something better, while the reverse fails.

questions.q: What happens at Pixar when a project fails?
a: The whole team shares responsibility, not one person
The director is fired immediately
The failure is hidden from the staff
The project is handed over to outsiders
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Pixar never points a finger at an individual, so blame is divided across the team.

questions.q: Why does shared failure make employees more creative?
a: They feel safe taking risks without taking all the blame
They compete harder for promotions
They avoid difficult projects entirely
They receive bigger bonuses for success
questions.why: The summary says people take more risks when a screw-up will be shared rather than blamed on one person.

questions.q: Why did Pixar replace its long rectangular meeting table?
a: It made people stiff and less willing to speak
It was too small for the whole team
It blocked the projector screen
It had been damaged in a fire
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the formal table with place cards made people tense, so a simple square table worked better.

questions.q: What freedom does Pixar give its tools department?
a: Two days a month to tinker with personal projects
A yearly budget for new equipment
Permission to work from home full time
A shared studio for group art
questions.why: The summary mentions that the tools team gets two days a month for personal experiments, much like Google.
